colors.note: Terrain park green and black, chosen by hand. The site uses inconsistent colours, so nothing on it is authoritative.

photos.alt: The wooden entrance sign at Wild Mountain, the name in blue and green with an eagle, and a CarbonNeutral Certified banner beneath it.
photos.caption: The sign on the way in.

photos.alt: David going down in the pond skim at Wild Mountain, mid-wipeout in a spray of green water, a crowd watching from the fence and the lift tower behind.
photos.caption: The pond skim, not cleared.

photos.alt: A blue and gold sign at Wild Mountain reading Cold? You Betcha!, framed by two spruces with the car park behind.
photos.caption: Cold? You Betcha.

photos.alt: A snowboard standing in a wooden rack outside the chalet at Wild Mountain, skis either side and slush underfoot.
photos.caption: In the rack outside the chalet.

photos.alt: Wild Mountain open on a thin strip of man-made snow at its preseason opening, low sun behind the hill, a few riders on the surface lift and grass showing at the edges.
photos.caption: Preseason opening, November 2025.

photos.alt: Wild Mountain under the lights at night, the chairlift running and tracked-out snow across the base area.
photos.caption: Under the lights.

photos.alt: Fresh corduroy at the top of a run at Trollhaugen, blue lift towers either side and Wisconsin farmland in the valley below.
photos.caption: Fresh corduroy, top of the hill.

photos.alt: Trollhaugen at dusk from above the base, runs lit, a terrain park on the right, skiers and boarders on the snow.
photos.caption: Lights on, park to the right.

photos.alt: A neon Trollhaugen sign in mixed colours on the gable of the wooden chalet at night.
photos.caption: The neon on the chalet.

photos.alt: A snowboard laid on a wooden tool bench under a sign reading Tool Bench, tools provided by the Trollhaugen Ski and Snowboard Shop, with leather gloves and a brush beside it.
photos.caption: The tool bench outside the shop.

photos.alt: A Trollhaugen lift ticket reading Valhalla, JAN 16 2026, Full Night.
photos.caption: Valhalla, Full Night, 16 January 2026.

colors.note: Park purple and orange, chosen by hand. Shares threeriversparks.org with Elm Creek, so site CSS cannot tell the two hills apart.

photos.alt: A snowboarder riding a feature in the terrain park at Hyland Hills under a clear blue sky, bare oaks behind.
photos.caption: The park, bluebird.

photos.alt: David in a helmet and a football shirt at Hyland Hills in June, riders on cached snow kept over for the event, rails and boxes set across it and green trees behind.
photos.caption: Cached snow, saved for a June event.

photos.alt: A rail set in the snow at Hyland Hills on a flat grey day, a group waiting at the top by the lift shack and pines behind.
photos.caption: Flat light, rail in the middle of the run.

photos.alt: A leather mitten worn through at the palm with the lining pulled out, held up at night with the lit hill behind.
photos.caption: Rope laps...

photos.alt: The view from the top of Buck Hill on a bright day, the chairlift on the right and the Twin Cities plain, a lake and a highway spread out below.
photos.caption: The metro from the top.

photos.alt: The terrain park at Buck Hill under a blue sky, a groomer parked mid-slope, blue and orange fencing and a black tube feature on the snow.
photos.caption: Park build, groomer still on it.

photos.alt: Riders and skiers at the top of Buck Hill at sunset, a snowmaking gun beside them and the sun low over the treeline.
photos.caption: Sunset from the top.

photos.alt: Snowed-in patio tables and chairs at Buck Hill at night, seen through glass, with the lit runs and the chairlift behind.
photos.caption: The patio, mid-storm.

photos.alt: The clock tower at the base of Buck Hill on an overcast day, with a sign listing the ticket office, ski patrol, chalets, the school and the tubing area.
photos.caption: The clock tower at the base.

giants-ridge.name: Giants Ridge
notes: The terrain park opens later than the hill does, usually by a week or two. An opening date here is lifts and runs, not park.

spirit-mountain.name: Spirit Mountain
notes: Opens in stages, every year on record: a single run or three in late November, then full hours in the second week of December. The gap runs a fortnight or more and is the hill's normal pattern, not a bad winter.
